# Clonal Hematopoiesis

Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) is the expansion of a blood stem cell clone carrying somatic mutations, most often in DNMT3A, TET2 and ASXL1, without a blood cancer. It becomes common with age. Because most cell-free DNA comes from blood cells, CH mutations appear in plasma and look like low-frequency somatic variants.

## Definition

> [!info]
> In this group the same CH variant calls play two opposite roles: in the MRD study they are noise to remove, in the Northvale cohort they are the exposure being studied. One callset, two uses, two different error costs.

We call CH from buffy coat DNA with one caller, developed in the [[clonal-hematopoiesis-filter|CH filter]] project and used for the Northvale subcohort calls ([[ch-subcohort-variant-calls]]): a somatic variant in a curated list of CH genes ([[ch-filter-gene-list]]), kept with flags from 0.5% VAF. Each project then applies its own threshold: 0.5% in buffy coat for the MRD filter, 2% (classical CHIP) as primary definition in the cohort analysis.

## Two Roles

**Noise in MRD.** In the [[pancreatic-cfdna-mrd-study|Pancreatic cfDNA MRD Study]], a post-operative plasma variant that comes from a blood clone would be a false molecular recurrence. The [[clonal-hematopoiesis-filter|Clonal Hematopoiesis Filter]] removes it. In our 60-patient matched pilot, 31% of plasma variants that passed the caller were present in buffy coat ([[ch-buffy-coat-pilot-results-2026-01]]). Here the costly error is keeping a CH variant: it tells a patient their cancer may be back. So the filter is tuned for sensitivity to CH, and a lower threshold (0.5% in buffy coat) applies.

**Exposure in the cohort.** In [[ch-cancer-risk-analysis|CH Cancer Risk Analysis]], led by [[lucas-brandt|Lucas Brandt]], CH at baseline in 6,000 Northvale participants is the exposure, and incident solid cancers are the outcome. Here the costly error is misclassifying a participant's exposure. The analysis therefore uses the stricter 2% VAF CHIP definition as primary and 1% as secondary ([[should-ch-be-defined-at-vaf-2-or-1-percent]]), and adjusts for smoking and age.

## Why One Callset

Both projects run the same caller, versioned together, and share calls in both directions:

- Northvale buffy coat calls from the cohort analysis are the main input to the MRD [[panel-of-normals]] ([[ch-panel-of-normals-v1]]): a variant that recurs in healthy older adults is likely CH when it appears in a St Aldric patient's plasma.
- St Aldric buffy coat calls from the pilot feed back into the cohort project as an external check of call quality at low VAF, because the St Aldric samples were sequenced deeper.

Sharing saves cost and makes the two projects consistent: a variant cannot be called CH in one and not in the other without a documented threshold difference. The risk is coupling. A caller change requested by one project changes the other's inputs, so call releases are frozen and versioned (the Northvale release is calls-v1.0, frozen 2026-05-08) and each project records which caller version it used. [[hannah-lindqvist|Hannah Lindqvist]] and Lucas co-own the release notes.

## Where It Matters

- Whether matched buffy coat sequencing (about 180 EUR per sample) is still needed or a panel of normals is enough: [[do-we-still-need-matched-buffy-coat-sequencing]].
- How big the panel of normals must be: [[how-large-must-the-ch-panel-of-normals-be]].
- Reviewer 1 on the [[mrd-manuscript|MRD Manuscript]] asked how CH was excluded ([[mrd-manuscript-decision-2026-07-14]]).

## Evidence We Lean On

- Large paired plasma and buffy coat profiling shows CH variants are frequent in clinically reportable genes, including TP53 and KRAS, and increase with age ([[magee-2025-cfdna-variants-tumour-or-ch-origin]]).
- Plasma-only approaches: a fragmentomics-based variant origin model ([[brown-2025-fragmentomic-variant-origin]]) and an open machine-learning classifier ([[arango-argoty-2025-metach-cfdna-ch-variants]]).
- A clinical case of repeated false-positive ctDNA surveillance from CH ([[spoor-2021-false-positive-ctdna-ch]]).
- CH can also appear as copy-number changes in cfDNA, not only point mutations ([[tuveri-2025-cfdna-cna-clonal-hematopoiesis]]).

## Caveats

Tumour-informed variants override the filter: if a variant was found in the resected tumour, it is kept even when it is also in buffy coat at low VAF, because pancreatic tumours can carry TP53 changes shared with a blood clone only by coincidence. That rule was argued at the [[ch-filter-design-meeting-2025-11-05|2025-11-05 design meeting]] and has affected four patients so far.

See also [[matched-normal-sequencing-is-cheaper-than-false-recurrence]].
